title: Replit vs Lovable
summary: Replit vs Lovable: builders evaluating development and live-app operating responsibility together.

sections.heading: Include day-two work
paragraphs: After the first prototype, add a migration, fix a failing request and rehearse a rollback. Record which operational responsibilities remain yours. A successful first build is only one part of this evaluation.

sections.heading: Budget the running application
paragraphs: List database, compute, storage, traffic and third-party services separately. Ask for the same billing period and expected workload in both candidates before using cost as the deciding factor.

sections.heading: When neither is a fit
paragraphs: If your required security, data location or operating environment is not supported by current evidence, pause the purchase. Use the sources below to resolve the missing constraint before accepting a recommendation.

verdict: Trial the complete app lifecycle in each candidate. Replit's public monthly and annual-billed Core base prices are recorded, but checkout-specific charges and complete app costs remain open, so no fixed-cost winner is justified.
bestFor: Builders evaluating development and live-app operating responsibility together
notFor: Buyers needing a fixed-cost winner before account-specific charges and full application costs are confirmed
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.

pros.text: Replit describes Agent as a workflow for planning, creating, checking, fixing and deploying an application, with project checkpoints documented separately.
Lovable documents code synchronization with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket for a repository-based handoff.

cons.text: Replit checkpoints are in-platform snapshots and do not demonstrate a separate export, deployment or recovery path.
Lovable credit usage covers build and runtime categories; a complete budget needs the actual project’s build, hosting and service usage.

faqs.question: Are Replit checkpoints and Lovable Git sync the same kind of handoff?
faqs.answer: No. Replit documents Git repository recovery and in-platform checkpoints; its provider-import guide says secrets, data or services may need separate setup. Lovable describes code sync to Git providers and separately calls for service migration planning. Neither statement is a completed migration test.

faqs.question: Does syncing Lovable code move its database and hosted services?
faqs.answer: The documentation treats database and service migration as separate work. Include those systems in an export and recovery rehearsal.

faqs.question: What should I verify about Lovable model training before sending project code?
faqs.answer: Its 2026-09-15 Privacy Policy says Customer Content and Usage Data may be used for training, with a free settings opt-out that takes effect prospectively on any plan; it excludes Business/Enterprise content and usage data and app end-user data. The August 2026 Terms and November 2025 DPA distinguish data scopes differently, so verify the actual workspace agreement and setting.

faqs.question: Does choosing an EU Lovable Cloud region keep all project data in the EU?
faqs.answer: Lovable says Lovable Cloud offers EU, US and Asia Pacific regions and that selected-region Cloud data does not move across regions by default. Its Privacy Policy also says Lovable and service providers process Personal Data in multiple countries, including the US. This does not establish the actual workspace selection or locations for connected services and model providers.

faqs.question: Does Replit's AI Integrations page establish local-model support for Replit Agent?
faqs.answer: Not from the reviewed docs. Replit describes AI Integrations as provider API access configured for the apps being built: managed credentials are billed to Replit credits at provider prices, while a developer's own API key is billed by the provider. A separate Model selector page describes model choice for Replit Agent itself. Neither page documents a local model or endpoint for Replit Agent, so local-model support remains unverified rather than being marked unsupported. No account, endpoint, integration or model was tested.

faqs.question: Can I self-host the Lovable platform as well as an app built with it?
faqs.answer: Lovable's hosting guide says the platform (editor and AI agent) is managed and cannot be self-hosted or deployed inside a customer VPC. Apps built with it can run on infrastructure you operate. This distinguishes application hosting from running the Lovable platform; no account or deployment was checked.
